Opens a commissioning window on a Matter device Indigo already controls, so another ecosystem (Apple Home, Alexa, Google, Home Assistant) can add it too — without removing it from Indigo.

Opens a pairing window so an ecosystem (Apple Home, Alexa, Google, SmartThings) can add the devices Indigo exports as Matter accessories.
The pairing code and a link to a QR page are written to the Indigo EVENT LOG when you click below — Indigo dialogs cannot display a code that is generated as you press the button.
A Matter pairing code is not permanent: once the first ecosystem has paired, that code stops working and each further ecosystem needs a new window. Expect an "uncertified accessory" warning in every ecosystem — that is normal, and the same warning Homebridge produces.
The bridge only runs while at least one device is exported, so add something in "Manage Matter Exports…" first.
Window stays open for (seconds):
Field.Description: Matter allows 180 to 900 (3 to 15 minutes). 900 is the maximum and the default.

Removes ONE ecosystem's pairing from the Matter bridge. Every accessory Indigo exports disappears from that ecosystem, along with the names, rooms, scenes and automations you built on them there. Other ecosystems are unaffected.
This is the export side only. Matter devices that Indigo CONTROLS are not affected, and no Indigo device is changed or deleted.
If you unpair the LAST ecosystem the bridge resets itself completely and starts advertising for commissioning again — the same outcome as "Reset Matter Bridge Pairings…".

Deletes the installed Matter controller (matter-server) package (~/indigo-matter/node_modules) and reinstalls it fresh, then restarts. Your commissioned devices are NOT affected — the fabric/storage is left untouched. Use this if matter-server won't start after an upgrade (e.g. a wedged install or a "Storage is locked" error).
I understand this reinstalls matter-server (devices/pairings are kept).

Removes the installed indigo-matter-bridge package from ~/indigo-matter and installs it fresh. Your ecosystem pairings and the exported accessories' identities are NOT affected — they live in the bridge's storage folder, which this never touches, and neither is matter-server.
Use this if the Matter bridge will not start after an upgrade and a plain "Install/update" has not fixed it.
I understand this reinstalls the bridge (pairings are kept).

Stops the Matter bridge process and removes its LaunchAgent, so it does not come back when this Mac restarts.
Your ecosystem pairings and your export list are NOT changed. Exported accessories will show as unavailable in Apple Home, Alexa and Google until the bridge runs again — which it does by itself the next time you add or change an export.
You normally never need this: the bridge starts and stops with your export list. It is here for the case where you want the process gone now — before disabling the plugin, for instance, which otherwise leaves it running with nothing to control it.
I understand exported accessories go unavailable until the bridge runs again.

Restoring REPLACES the current fabric and restarts matter-server. If the backup includes the Matter bridge node's storage, that is restored too — if the bridge node is running it is stopped and started around the swap; a stopped bridge stays stopped. The current fabric (and bridge storage, if restored) is moved aside, not deleted, so a bad restore is reversible. Requires 'Manage LaunchAgent' to be on.
Backup to restore:
I understand this replaces the current fabric (and the Matter bridge node's storage, if the backup has it) and will restart matter-server.

Use this ONLY when the plugin says the bridge node is refusing to export because its endpoint-number map is unreadable. The map is the bridge's safety record of which Matter accessory number belongs to which Indigo device; rebuilding it discards the unreadable record and adopts whatever numbers exist now as the new one.
Rebuilding renumbers NOTHING, so it cannot itself duplicate accessories. What you see afterwards depends on which fault brought you here:
- If only the map file was damaged, the accessories keep their numbers, no paired ecosystem (Apple Home, Alexa, Google) sees any further change, and the rebuild simply clears the refusal.
- If the bridge's Matter storage was lost, your ecosystems are ALREADY holding accessories under the old numbers — those are dead, you have to delete them by hand, and any names, rooms, scenes and automations built on them are lost. That damage was done by the storage loss; rebuilding accepts it rather than causing it.
The unreadable file is kept beside the new one as endpoint-map.json.corrupt-<timestamp>; if you have a backup of the original, restoring that is better than rebuilding. No pairing is touched, and no Indigo device is changed.
If the bridge node is NOT refusing, this does nothing useful and is refused: there is no fault to recover from, and a rebuild would discard the retained endpoint numbers of every device you are not currently exporting — the ones that make re-adding a device restore the same accessory rather than create a second one.
I understand this replaces the endpoint-number record and cannot be undone.

Moves a live exported accessory to a different Indigo device — for replaced hardware, a module moved to new gear, or a device rebuilt under a new id. Nothing is removed and nothing is re-paired: Apple Home and every other paired ecosystem keep the accessory's room, name, scenes and automations, because from their side nothing happened. The old device stays in Indigo, no longer exported.
A ROLE CHANGE is not what this is for — export the replacement device normally instead, and it becomes a new accessory. A device that cannot take the source accessory's role is refused below.

Field.Label: If the device you pick above already has its own accessory (marked ●), migrating removes THAT accessory from every ecosystem and puts the migrated one in its place instead.
I understand this moves the accessory to a different Indigo device.

Hands a left-behind Matter accessory identity to a different Indigo device. The accessory returns under its original identity and number, and no duplicate is created — but an ecosystem that has already processed the removal (Apple Home does within moments) will show it in the Default Room under a default name, and any scene or automation that referenced it must be rebuilt. If the old Indigo device still exists, "Migrate an exported accessory…" (above) is the right tool instead: the identity never lapses there, so no ecosystem ever processes a removal, and room, name, scenes and automations survive.
An accessory is left behind when the Indigo device that exported it is deleted, or when it stops being exported. It can only be re-adopted onto a device that can take the SAME role as the accessory it is inheriting; a device that cannot is refused below — export it normally instead, and it becomes a new accessory.
A ROLE CHANGE is not recoverable this way. Changing a role removes the old accessory and adds a new one (issue #240), and the old one's accessory number is retired on purpose — re-adopting it would put an old-role accessory back under a number your ecosystems have already processed a removal for. Those accessories are not offered below.
Left-behind accessory:
Left-behind accessories your ecosystems still remember.

Removes EVERY ecosystem pairing from the Matter bridge and starts advertising for commissioning again. Apple Home, Alexa, Google and anything else you have paired will lose all of the accessories Indigo exports, and you will have to pair the bridge again from scratch.
This is the export side only. Matter devices that Indigo CONTROLS are not affected, and no Indigo device is changed or deleted.
Endpoint numbers are kept, so re-pairing the same ecosystems restores the same accessory identities where it can.
